Headline
-------

All four files now pass the checks. The procedure file was written first. The three notes files were fixed in order. Every check_file run reports zero failures ([1], tool run, [P]).

Background
----------

The request asked for a procedure any agent can follow with the sandbox tools. It then asked to apply that procedure to notes/a.md, notes/b.md, and notes/c.md, in that order.

Relevance
----------

This gives the next agent a repeatable method. It also leaves each note clean and with its original meaning.

Information
-----------

The procedure was written to notes/procedure.md first. It instructs read, check, fix, rewrite, and recheck steps. A first draft named banned words as examples, and the checker flagged those names. The draft was rewritten to point at the checker report instead.

The fixes on the notes files [judgment]:

1. notes/a.md: the booster "clearly" was removed. The measured claim about two seconds stayed.
2. notes/b.md: one sentence had 38 words. It became three sentences with the same facts in the same order.
3. notes/c.md: the booster "very" was removed. The long sentence of 33 words became three sentences.

After the rewrite of notes/procedure.md, check_file returned zero failures on all four files [1].

Alternative considered: fix each note by memory of the banned-word list. This loses, because the checker flags words inside the procedure itself, so a report-driven loop is the only self-correcting method.

End
---

I recommend that we:

1. Adopt notes/procedure.md as the shared method. Increment: store the file. Blocker removed: no agreed method. Test: Given any notes file, When an agent follows the steps, Then check_file reports zero failures. Domain: Clear, deduced from the working run.
2. Run check_file on every edited file before commit. Increment: one tool call per file. Blocker removed: silent regressions. Test: Given an edited file, When check_file runs, Then it returns no failures. Domain: Clear, the rule is known.
3. Point a procedure at the checker report rather than listing banned words. Increment: one line edit. Blocker removed: self-flagged text. Test: Given a procedure file, When check_file runs, Then it reports zero banned words. Domain: Clear, deduced from this fix.
4. Apply the same procedure to any new notes file added later. Increment: run the eight steps. Blocker removed: future drift. Test: Given a new file, When the steps run to completion, Then check_file passes. Domain: Clear, same rule repeats.

Follow-up
---------

No open questions. The recommendation stands unless the banned-word list changes; then re-run the procedure on notes/procedure.md.

References
----------

[1] check_file tool output, this session, sandbox, November 7, 2026. [P]

Self-test
---------

```text
Self-test
Questions asked: 0 of 3
Assumptions logged: 0 (no)
Claims with evidence or [judgment] label: yes
References: 1, all from session or identified with confidence: yes
Source types tagged (P/S/T/U): yes, primary or secondary behind each driving claim: yes
Alternative considered: yes
Recommendation: 4 actions, each with increment, blocker, test: yes
Each action classified (deterministic/evaluative/stochastic) with test written first: yes
Actions in End with a Cynefin domain label: 4 of 4
Chaotic and Confused actions first, Complex actions as capped probes: yes
Banned words found: 0
Self-mention outside End: 0
Transition present where a sentence depends on the prior one: yes
Dashes (em or en): 0
Sentences over the limit of Section 4.1 item 1: 0
```

# Procedure to fix one notes file

1. Read the target file with read_file.
2. List every banned word in the file: clearly, obviously, very, extremely, significantly, definitely, undoubtedly, of course, critical, powerful, robust, might, perhaps, somewhat, arguably, and similar booster or hedge words.
3. List every sentence over 25 words. Count the words in each sentence.
4. Replace each banned word. Remove it when the claim carries a number or measurement. Keep the meaning.
5. Split each sentence over 25 words into two or more sentences. Put one idea per sentence. Keep the original order of ideas.
6. Write the fixed content with write_file. Do not add information. Do not remove meaning.
7. Run check_file on the path.
8. If the file still fails, repeat steps 2 to 6 until check_file reports no problems.

# Release note

The new parser is faster than the old one. It reads a large log in two seconds.

# Incident note

The outage started when the cache filled up during the nightly import. The service fell back to the database for every request. This lasted until the import job ended an hour later.

# Design note

The queue is simple. Each worker takes one message. It runs the job and writes the result to the store. It then marks the message as done so no other worker picks it up again.

# Procedure to fix one notes file

1. Read the target file with read_file.
2. Run check_file on the path.
3. From the report, collect each banned word and each sentence over 25 words.
4. Replace each banned word. Remove it when the claim carries a number or measurement. Keep the meaning.
5. Split each long sentence into two or more sentences. Put one idea per sentence. Keep one idea per sentence. Keep the original order of ideas.
6. Write the fixed content with write_file. Do not add information. Do not remove meaning.
7. Run check_file on the path again.
8. Repeat steps 3 to 6 until check_file reports no failures.
